label: <DEL> step when first token is v/h/e/x/i/j/u/m/3/d, plus original-phase q
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 68% of activation mass and the top examples sit on the <DEL> input (37% of delimiter steps are active, 7.4x lift). Whether it fires and how strongly at <DEL> depends on the first original token, which is the token about to be output: v, h, e, x, i, j, u, m, 3, d give 3-6x lift and the strongest activations. A last original token of l/p before <DEL> also seems to boost it. Second component: q inputs during the original phase (29% rate, 16% of mass), most reliable at t<=2 (precision 0.72). There is weak spillover onto the first copy step (recall_idx 1, 13% of mass), usually smaller than the <DEL> activation. Almost silent late in the copy phase and on most other letters and digits in the original phase. The first-token gating at <DEL> is graded, not a clean set, so precision and recall are both incomplete (dev F1 0.58, mass recall 0.65).
